title: 1.4 Major Geological Processes
description: Endogenic and exogenic forces, folding, faulting, earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanism. Hard level.

questions.question: How fast can a tsunami travel in deep water?
options: Forces that originate inside the Earth
A crack in the Earth crust

questions.question: What share of earthquake energy comes from the Circum-Pacific Belt?
Where do deep-focus earthquakes commonly occur?
options: Land between two faults that has sunk down
In Benioff zones along subducted plates
Forces that originate inside the Earth
questions.correctAnswer: In Benioff zones along subducted plates

questions.question: What share of seismic energy comes from shallow-focus earthquakes?
options: A crack in the Earth crust

questions.question: How does a vent differ from a fissure?
options: A vent builds a cone; a fissure builds a plateau
Land between two faults that has sunk down
They have larger amplitude and travel along the surface
A giant ocean wave generated by underwater earthquakes
questions.correctAnswer: A vent builds a cone; a fissure builds a plateau

questions.question: Which volcano has a low, broad profile formed by fluid basaltic lava?
Which volcano is a steep cone of alternating lava and pyroclastic layers?
Which volcano is an example of an active volcano in Ethiopia?
What share of active volcanoes lies in the Pacific Ring of Fire?
Why are surface waves responsible for much destructive shaking?
options: A fracture forms and one limb is pushed forward over the other
They have larger amplitude and travel along the surface
The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements
Shock waves released by shifting rock during an earthquake
questions.correctAnswer: They have larger amplitude and travel along the surface
